newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish ten-year bond yield hits low, crown steady.
newsitem.headline: Swedish ten-year bond yield hits low, crown steady.

text.p: 1550 GMT - The Swedish ten-year bond yield dropped to an all-time low on the last settlement day of 1996, while year-end effects braked falls in the shorter end.

Trade was seen calm on Monday, a shortened trade session, as many take off for the Christmas holidays. * Six-month T-bill rate steady at 3.88 percent * Ten-year bond yield down seven basis points to 6.76 percent * Mark steady against crown at 4.3900 versus 4.3945 Thursday
Longer debt yields closed at an all-time low on Friday in thin pre-holiday trade, helped by stronger foreign markets, while shorter maturities closed flat because of year-end effects, dealers said.
A better-than-expected Swedish November producer price index (PPI) added to the bullish sentiment.
"The PPI figure was very good, even if you look at its different components. This played its part," one dealer said.
Swedish November PPI fell 0.4 percent for a year-on-year fall of 3.8 percent compared to expectations for a flat figure.
Ten-year bond yields fell seven basis points to 6.76 percent and the spread between Swedish and German long yields narrowed three basis points to 94.
Six-month T-bill rates closed flat at 3.88 percent and the crown was stable at 4.3900 against the mark compared to 4.3945 late on Thursday.

"Trade in Swedish crowns was active considering the time of the year. We've seen both position adjustments and commercial flows from the major export companies. The fact the bond market has done well has lent support," a chief dealer said.
